title: Demurrage and Detention Free Time: Dangerous-Goods Uplift on Demurrage Day Rates
content:
## Clause

Where the booking under which a container moves has dangerous goods as its cargo type, each demurrage day rate on the Demurrage and Detention Free Time record is raised by the product's dangerous-goods uplift percentage, applied to that rate itself. Where the booking's cargo type is anything else, demurrage day rates carry no uplift at all.

## Branches

| Booking cargo type | Uplift applied to each demurrage day rate |
|---|---|
| dangerous goods | the product's uplift percentage of the rate |
| any other | none |

## Points of judgement

- The uplift is taken on each demurrage day's own rate, at whichever slab and rate class that day is priced.
- The percentage used is the one belonging to the product on the record.
- The test turns on the booking's cargo type as the booking record states it.

## Illustration (hypothetical rate and percentage)

A demurrage day rate of 90.00 on a dangerous-goods booking, under a product whose uplift is assumed to be 40 percent, is raised by 36.00 to 126.00. The same day on a booking of another cargo type stays at 90.00.
